## POST `/api/2.58/volume-groups`

**Tier:** T1+ (check: some POSTs are actions)  

Creates a volume group. The volume group itself does not contain any meaningful content; instead, it acts as a container that is used to organize volumes. Once a volume group has been created, volumes can be created inside the volume group or moved into and out of the volume group.

**Request body** (required): `VolumeGroupPost`

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | string (read-only) | A globally unique, system-generated ID. The ID cannot be modified and cannot refer to another resource. |
| `name` | string | A user-specified name. The name must be locally unique and can be changed. |
| `destroyed` | boolean (read-only) | If set to `true`, destroys a volume group. If set to `false`, recovers a destroyed volume group. If not specified, defaults to `false`. |
| `priority_adjustment` | `_priorityAdjustment` |  |
| `qos` | `_qos` |  |

| `time_remaining` | integer (int64) (read-only) | The amount of time left until the destroyed volume group is permanently eradicated, measured in milliseconds. |
| `volume_count` | integer (int64) (read-only) | The number of volumes in the volume group. |

**Responses:** `200` OK → `VolumeGroupResponse`

## PATCH `/api/2.58/volume-groups`

**Tier:** T2 (T3 if it destroys, eradicates, disables or overwrites)  

Modifies a volume group. You can rename, destroy, recover, or set QoS limits for a volume group. To rename a volume group, set `name` to the new name. To destroy a volume group, set `destroyed=true`. To recover a volume group that has been destroyed and is pending eradication, set `destroyed=false`. Sets the bandwidth and IOPS limits of a volume group through the respective `bandwidth_limit` and `iops_limit` parameter. The `ids` or `names` parameter is required, but they cannot be set together. Sets the priority adjustment for a volume group using the `priority_adjustment_operator` and…

## DELETE `/api/2.58/volume-groups`

**Tier:** T3  

Deletes a volume group that has been destroyed and is pending eradication. Eradicated volume groups cannot be recovered. Volume groups are destroyed through the PATCH method. The `ids` or `names` parameter is required, but they cannot be set together.
